17:
[Partial translation]
"And every living soul creeping upon the earth". These are Yisrael that they are surely soul, that they are living and are called one nation in the land. "That the water swarmed to their species". That they work in Torah. "And all the bird of wing to its' kind." These are the righteous that are in them. And this is why they are living soul. Another explanation, "And every bird of wing", like that we said, these are those (earlier 34:1) "messengers of world".

Rabbi Abba says, "soul of life", that they are (a.p. they are) Yisrael, because they are children of the Holy one Blessed be He (a.p. children to the Holy one Blessed be He). And their holy souls come from him. The souls of the rest of the nations worshipers of aku"m from which place are they? Rabbi Elazar says from those left sides that are unholy to them they have souls. And because of this they are all unholy, and they make unholy he who becomes close with them.
18:
[Partial translation]
Rabbi Simeon was journeying to Tiberias, and there were with him, Rabbi Jose, Rabbi Jehuda, and Rabbi Hiya. While on the way, they saw Rabbi Pinchus coming to meet them. After exchanging greetings, they all sat down under a great shady tree by a hillside. Then Rabbi Pinchus said: "now that we are seated, please instruct me further in the Secret Doctrine, that you are teaching daily."

Then Rabbi Simeon said: "It is written, 'and he went on his journeys from the south to Bethel unto the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Hai' (Gen. 13:3). It says, 'He went on his journeys' instead of 'his journey.' Why is that? There is a reference not only to his own journeying, but also that of the Schekina, who always went with Jacob, and therefore we learn that every person needs to be male and female at all time, for the sake of his faith, he ought not to think or imagine that the Schekina forsakes him in any way.

See, it has been said, a man ought always to cleave to his wife that the Schekina may always be with him, yet it is possible to go alone on a journey and the Schekina will still be with him. And when doing so he ought to direct his prayer to the Holy One that this may be, and in this way the male and female will always be associated in union with oneself.
20:
[Partial translation]
Rabbi Shimon said: Adam separated from his wife for 130 years. During all of those years, he produced spirits and demons in the world on account of that power of impurity that he had absorbed into himself. Once that impurity had left him, he went back and became jealous for his wife, and he fathered a son [from her]. Hence it is written: and he produced [a son] in his likeness according to his image (Genesis 5:3).
